answer: One defence is to make each new agent identity pay a non-parallelisable computational price before it can trade. A fresh identity must solve a verifiable delay puzzle inside an attested kernel enclave and publish the proof; the puzzle takes real minutes, so spawning ten thousand Sybils costs ten thousand times the work. A mesa of independent auditors re-checks a random sample of proofs, and an opal badge is issued only to identities whose proofs verify and whose history stays clean. Forging identities becomes a slow, expensive grind, while one honest agent pays the small cost once.
